summary: Feed s118_double to IDS is degraded: 27.5% of frames are sliced to 128 bytes (887/3228) and 97.2% remain VXLAN-encapsulated (3138/3228), both blocking full-payload inspection required by IDS.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing/snaplen is configured to ~128 bytes, likely to save bandwidth to the 1 Gbps IDS port. Broker is truncating frames before delivery instead of forwarding full frames.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_full_payload=true for signature matching and stream reassembly; truncated frames lose L4 payload so IDS will miss exploits, fail to detect application-layer attacks, and generate incomplete sessions.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires full payload; disable slicing or set snaplen >= max_frame_bytes (1518) so complete packets reach IDS for detection.

findings.root_cause: Traffic is sourced from a VXLAN overlay and the packet broker is forwarding encapsulated frames without decapsulation. 97.2% of frames still carry VXLAN headers on the tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS sees only outer VXLAN/IP/UDP headers and cannot parse inner Ethernet/IP/TCP and payload; signatures never match inner traffic, causing near-total detection blindness.

recommended_fix.why: Strip VXLAN encapsulation on the packet broker to present inner original frames to IDS for correct parsing and detection coverage.
